findings.message: When a git/source install lacks the bundled ao-update.sh, `ao update` falls back to `handleNpmUpdate(opts, "npm-global")`, which installs `@aoagents/ao@latest` globally from npm instead of updating the checkout. Source-checkout user (launcher installed via `npm link` of packages/ao) whose dist/assets lacks ao-update.sh (built with plain `tsc`, or assets copy skipped) runs `ao update` in a TTY and confirms. `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest` replaces the global `@aoagents/ao` symlink with the registry build, so `ao` silently stops running their checkout. If the checkout version is already >= the npm latest, the user sees 'Already on latest' and the source is never pulled. pnpm users are also hard-coded to npm. The new test locks in this behavior.

run_smoke_tests runs `node $REPO_ROOT/packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js`, but the launcher package is now `packages/ao/bin/ao.js` (renamed in 4fcdc674), so smoke tests always fail under `set -e`. In a real checkout, `ao update` without --skip-smoke does the full fetch, clean, rebuild, and npm link, then fails with 'Cannot find module .../packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js'. The script exits 1, executeScriptCommand calls process.exit(1), and invalidateCache never runs. `ao update --smoke-only` always fails. Tests miss this because update-script fixtures create the stale directory.

check_runtime_sanity (touched by this diff) still checks `$REPO_ROOT/packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js`, which does not exist in the repo; the launcher is `packages/ao/bin/ao.js`. Every `ao doctor` on a real source checkout prints 'FAIL launcher entrypoint is missing. Fix: reinstall from a clean checkout' and exits 1. The doctor-script fixture `createHealthyRepo` creates both `packages/ao` and `packages/agent-orchestrator/bin/ao.js` (doctor-script.test.ts:35-43), which hides the bug.

The fallback `REPO_ROOT=$(cd $(dirname BASH_SOURCE)/.. && pwd)` assumed the script lived at `<repo>/scripts/`. After the move it resolves to `packages/cli/{src,dist}/assets`, not the repo root. If a failed rebuild leaves dist removed, the recovery path is running the script directly (`bash packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-update.sh`). It then cds into `.../src/assets`, runs git and pnpm from there, and fails at `cd "$REPO_ROOT/packages/ao"` (`.../assets/packages/ao` does not exist). Smoke-test paths are wrong too. Before the move, `bash scripts/ao-update.sh` worked standalone.

ao-doctor.sh's default REPO_ROOT (`dirname BASH_SOURCE/..`) now resolves to `.../assets` instead of the repo or package root. The new layout heuristic at lines 33-39 then always picks source-checkout when the script runs without AO_REPO_ROOT. Running `bash packages/cli/dist/assets/scripts/ao-doctor.sh` directly, or any wrapper that doesn't set AO_REPO_ROOT, reports FAIL for `.../assets/node_modules`, `.../assets/packages/core/dist/index.js`, and so on, then exits 1 on a healthy install. A packaged install run directly is never detected as package-install. Docs (docs/design-onboarding-improvements.html) still point to scripts/ao-doctor.sh.

classifyInstallPath dropped the `scripts/ao-update.sh` checkout marker without adding a replacement, so any non-node_modules path whose 4th ancestor has a `.git` is classified as `git`. A CLI build vendored or copied into another git repo (e.g. `<other-repo>/tools/ao/dist/lib/update-check.js`) is classified `git`. `ao update` then runs ao-update.sh with REPO_ROOT set to that unrelated repo: `git pull --ff-only origin main`, `pnpm install`, `pnpm --filter ... clean`, and `cd packages/ao && npm link` all run against the wrong repository. The removed tests had covered the '.git exists but not an AO checkout' case.

In the new fallback, `--smoke-only` (documented as 'Run smoke tests without fetching or rebuilding') is ignored and the npm update flow runs, which can prompt for and perform `npm install -g`. The flow also prints '--skip-smoke and --smoke-only only apply to git source installs', which contradicts the git classification. A user on a git checkout with no bundled update script runs `ao update --smoke-only` to verify their install. Instead they get a version comparison and a prompt to run `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`. Accepting it changes the install, which is the opposite of what smoke-only promises. Previously, smoke-only never changed anything.

Using `cwd: process.cwd()` instead of the repo root adds a synchronous `process.cwd()` call that throws ENOENT when the shell's working directory has been deleted. The option is also redundant, since spawn already inherits the cwd. A user sits in an AO worktree that `ao` cleanup has removed and runs `ao doctor`. `process.cwd()` throws `ENOENT: uv_cwd` inside the Promise executor. Doctor catches it, prints the error, and skips every shell check (shellExitCode=1). Before this change the spawn used an explicit repo-root cwd. Omitting `cwd` avoids the throw.

The character class in `/[.*+?^${}()|[\\]\\\\]/g` closes at the first `\\]`, so the pattern only matches a special char followed by literal `\\]` and never escapes anything. The scripts dir path goes into `new RegExp` unescaped. Checked with node: '/tmp/a+b(c)/x.y/scripts'.replace(<test regex>) returns the input unchanged. A checkout path containing `+`, `(`, `[`, or `?` (e.g. `~/code/ao (copy)/`) makes the test fail or throw 'Invalid regular expression'. Unescaped `.` also matches any character, which weakens the assertion. Intended pattern: `/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g`.

getScriptPath now always uses the module-relative CLI_DIST_ROOT and ignores the AO_REPO_ROOT override. That override is still passed to the script, so the script version and the repo it acts on can come from different trees. A developer sets AO_REPO_ROOT=~/ao-dev to test a modified ao-update.sh or ao-doctor.sh in another checkout. The globally installed CLI runs its own bundled copy against ~/ao-dev, so their changes never run and the old script logic acts on the new tree. Before this change, resolveScriptPath used resolveRepoRoot(), so the override chose the script too.

Install layout is now decided in three places that can disagree: script-runner's node_modules check, update-check's classifyInstallPath (now .git-only), and this shell heuristic. The update.ts hasRepoScript fallback works around the mismatch instead of fixing classification. A source tarball without .git gives layout=source-checkout but install=unknown. npx gives layout=package-install but install=unknown. A stale dist gives install=git but no script, which hits the npm fallback. Each new case needs another special case. Simpler fix: have classifyInstallPath require the bundled `assets/scripts/ao-update.sh` (or `packages/cli/package.json`) next to `.git`, derive ScriptLayout from that one classifier, and drop the shell heuristic, since the TS caller always passes AO_SCRIPT_LAYOUT.

resolveScriptLayoutFromPath and resolveDefaultRepoRootFromPath repeat the `/node_modules/` / `\\node_modules\\` check and the `resolve(dirname(p), "../../../../")` repo-root walk from update-check.ts classifyInstallPath. Two copies of the same path heuristics must stay in sync. A fix to one (e.g. Windows separators, pnpm store layout) won't reach the other, so `ao doctor` and `ao update` can disagree about the same install. Reuse `classifyInstallPath` (or extract a shared `isNodeModulesPath`/`sourceRepoRootFrom` helper in update-check.ts).

The package-install branch checks that ao-doctor.sh exists (it is the running script) and that package.json and dist/index.js exist (required for the CLI to have started). It also FAILs on a missing ao-update.sh, which package installs never use, and checks dist/index.js again in check_runtime_sanity, which double-counts FAILs. These checks add output and maintenance without catching anything real. A missing dist/index.js produces two FAIL lines. Doctor exits 1 over a missing source-update script that npm/pnpm installs never call. Keep only the runtime `node dist/index.js --version` check.

Commit 76652c7c is titled 'Fix packaged doctor and update fallback', which breaks the repo CLAUDE.md rule 'Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `chore:`, `perf:`, `ci:`'. Violates /CLAUDE.md (Conventions → Commits). The subject has no `fix(cli):` prefix, unlike the sibling commits 89427ee5 and c2358798, which can break changelog and changeset tooling that keys on the prefix.
